topics: Helm chart/Operator vs simple Helm pack
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-01 15:00 UTC | Duration 46m
Attendees: Maya Patel, Liam Chen, Arjun Rao (Redwood) — Helena Ortiz, Marcus Li, Nina Park, Owen Brooks (SilverMist)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Liam and Arjun from SE. we planned this as a technical kickoff for the marketplace listing and a small quant pilot, so we'll cover packaging (helm), networking and security, then lab steps.

[00:18] Helena Ortiz: Great — thanks. we have limited windows for staging deploys during our month-end, so timeline matters.

[00:25] Liam Chen: Noted. rough agenda — 1) Helm packaging options (operator vs helm chart), 2) VPC / private deployment and KMS, 3) quantization tradeoffs and a pilot plan, 4) telemetry/observability for the marketplace listing.

[00:42] Marcus Li: Quick context: currently on GKE 1.24, internal CI deploys via ArgoCD, private subnets, egress through a NAT gateway. We'll need RBAC-limited kubeconfig for any Redwood lab access. Also we enforce customer-managed KMS for keys.

[01:05] Arjun Rao: Okay, that's helpful. from Redwood side we can do a Helm chart that supports a simple CRD operator later, but initial listing typically uses a packaged Helm chart + values file. That keeps the install light for marketplace customers.

[01:30] Nina Park: Security first — we insist on CMEK, audit logs, and no plaintext tokens. How does Redwood handle KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments?

[01:50] Liam Chen: We support both cloud KMS and customer-managed keys in our Private offering — in marketplace listings we include an integration guide showing how to register a KMS key and mount secrets via CSI. There's also an option to route token exchange through a KMS proxy. We will share the KMS runbook. (note: sometimes transcribed as "K-M-S runbook" or "K-M-S proxy")

[02:12] Owen Brooks: For the listing we'll need an ops doc describing SA roles and minimum permissions. Can you outline the least-privileged service account?

[02:25] Liam Chen: Yes — we'll produce a values file with example SA manifests. basic permissions are: create pods, list/watch endpoints, create configmaps/secrets (but secrets only if using CSI), and limited crd permissions if operator used. We'll add a readme for RBAC.

[02:44] Marcus Li: On networking — do you need inbound from public internet? Our staging cluster is private. how does Redwood connect to hosted control plane or marketplace telemetry?

[02:58] Arjun Rao: For Private mode there's a control-plane connector that can be configured to use egress only — calls outbound to Redwood for ops telemetry; no inbound required. For marketplace listing we provide an option to run a sidecar that posts metrics to a telemetry endpoint behind your VPC/NAT. We call this the "connector" in docs — sometimes transcribed as "connecter" or "conector".

[03:20] Helena Ortiz: Good — we prefer egress-only. we also need to keep logs for 13 months for compliance. what's the log retention story?

[03:30] Liam Chen: By default our agent ships logs to the customer's telemetry sink (you can configure S3 or a logging endpoint). For hosted listing we keep redwood-side telemetry short-lived, but you get a copy to your sink for retention. We'll add a section in the listing checklist for retention policies.

[03:46] Maya Patel: Switching to quantization pilot — Marcus, what latency and cost targets are you optimizing for?

[03:55] Marcus Li: For user-facing chat flows we need p99 under 300ms on our initial key path, and cost not to exceed a soft target of 0.8x of current token spend (we already run an internal LLM gateway). Those are soft but important.

[04:15] Arjun Rao: Good, that's doable to test. for quantization we want to try 4-bit and 8-bit variants on a curated prompt set. Redwood's runtime has quant-friendly kernels and KV cache behavior that helps with latency, but there are tradeoffs — sometimes 4-bit shows lower throughput for certain attention patterns. We'll recommend a small matrix.

[04:40] Nina Park: Are there known model/regression risks when quantizing? we need quality gates.

[04:48] Liam Chen: Yes — small accuracy/regression risks. we'll run evals with your prompt set and produce a quality delta report. Redwood Optimize suggestions will include prompt-level regression alerts. we'll attach an example eval harness.

[05:05] Owen Brooks: For the benchmark can you share the spreadsheet with fields you need?

[05:10] Arjun Rao: We'll share a baseline spreadsheet (latency tails, cost/token, output similarity metrics). please provide 20 representative prompts and a small set of acceptance criteria per prompt.

[05:22] Maya Patel: Let's talk packaging: are you open to us publishing a helm repo that SilverMist can include in cloud marketplaces as an upstream?

[05:30] Helena Ortiz: Yes, that's ideal. We also have internal policies that require helm charts to be signed and a reproducible build.

[05:40] Liam Chen: We can sign charts and provide reproducible build steps. for marketplace marketplace vendors often want a single tarball with values examples, a minimal operator (optional), and a test harness. We usually include a "listing-readme.md" with architecture diagrams — we'll draft that.

[05:58] Marcus Li: On the operator vs helm debate: operator adds convenience for lifecycle actions but increases surface area and RBAC. we might prefer a simple helm pack for listing and offer operator as opt-in later.

[06:15] Arjun Rao: That's the common pattern. initial release: helm-only with clear upgrade hooks; later introduce operator for live scaling and autoscaler integration.

[06:30] Nina Park: Any attention to quant libs and licensing? some quant kernels use third-party libs.

[06:38] Liam Chen: We'll document third-party libraries and their licenses in the BOM. Redwood's runtime picks optimized kernels but we can vendor open-source quant libs or build them into the container image for the marketplace bundle.

[06:55] Owen Brooks: Observability — we need traces and token-level cost. What hooks are available?

[07:05] Arjun Rao: Our agent exposes Prometheus metrics and an optional tracing span export (OTEL). We also surface per-request token cost in the payload and a token breakdown in the console. For marketplace we'll include a sample Grafana dashboard.

[07:25] Helena Ortiz: Great. small question: will the chart support multi-AZ deployments and node selectors for GPUs?

[07:35] Liam Chen: Yes — values include tolerations, nodeSelectors, and a GPU profile map. we also include a batch config for continuous batching options.

[07:48] Marcus Li: Regarding credentials, do we need to provide long-lived tokens? we prefer short-lived service accounts.

[07:56] Arjun Rao: You can use short-lived tokens via our workload identity flow or use a token broker pattern. We'll include examples for both in the runbook.

[08:10] Maya Patel: Can we sync on the pilot scope — what would success look like for both sides?

[08:18] Owen Brooks: For SilverMist: p99 < 300ms on primary prompt set, quality delta < 2% for core intents, and ability to deploy via our CI with the Helm pack.

[08:30] Marcus Li: And minimal infra changes — egress-only, CMEK, and no inbound ports.

[08:38] Liam Chen: From Redwood: validate quant 8-bit and 4-bit tradeoffs on your prompt set, demonstrate helm install and upgrade, and provide a listing-ready bundle and docs. we'll also surface cost delta numbers.

[08:54] Nina Park: On compliance: we'll need SOC2-to-SOC2 mappings for the connector and a summary of where data at-rest and in-transit resides.

[09:05] Arjun Rao: We'll provide a high-level map and redacted artifacts; for full SOC2 you'll need an NDA and process — we'll coordinate through legal.

[09:20] Maya Patel: Ok moving into the lab plan: propose a two-week pilot window. Week one: baseline benchmarks hosted in your staging cluster with Redwood helm chart installed. Week two: quant runs and regression evals.

[09:38] Marcus Li: That timing works if we get kubeconfig and values by 10/07.

[09:45] Liam Chen: We'll target Helm tarball and example values by 10/06. Also I'll upload a sample prometheus dashboard and the benchmark spreadsheet by then.

[09:55] Owen Brooks: Any blockers around marketplace certs? sometimes marketplaces require specific packaging for billing hooks.

[10:05] Liam Chen: We have marketplace packaging guidelines per provider; billing hooks depend on the marketplace — for example some need a metering endpoint. We'll include a small note and point to provider-specific docs.

[10:18] Helena Ortiz: Who owns the listing submission? we typically want to own the vendor account but need Redwood artifacts.

[10:26] Maya Patel: SilverMist can own the vendor profile; Redwood will hand off the listing bundle and a compliance package for upload. We'll include the listing checklist.

[10:40] (crosstalk) Marcus Li: quick — are there sample cost models?

[10:44] Arjun Rao: Yes, we'll model cost/token across quant levels and provide a table. it's approximate but useful for decisioning.

[10:55] Nina Park: small nit: ensure that the Helm chart does not include any hard-coded secrets or endpoints.

[11:02] Liam Chen: Absolutely — charts will be generic and read from values.

[11:10] Maya Patel: Let's summarize next steps — Liam uploads helm tarball, benchmark sheet and dashboard; Marcus and Nina share staging access and compliance questions; Maya circulates pilot SLOs and scoping template.

[11:30] Owen Brooks: Agreed. last Q — can we get a quick demo of the install flow next week?

[11:36] Maya Patel: Yes let's schedule a 30-min install demo / lab kickoff. I'll send invites after this call.

[11:45] Helena Ortiz: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.

[11:50] Maya Patel: Thanks all — talk soon.

End of transcript.
